payload.title: Filtering and Detrending with Pyleoclim
payload.summary: This Jupyter notebook introduces users to filtering and detrending methods using the Pyleoclim library. It demonstrates how to apply various signal processing techniques to benthic foraminifera δ18O data from the LR04 benthic stack. The notebook covers methods such as empirical mode decomposition (EMD), Savitzky-Golay filtering, and Lanczos filtering, providing visualizations of the original and processed data. The goal is to familiarize users with these methods and their arguments, enhancing their ability to process paleoclimate data.
goals: Become familiar with the various filtering methods and some of their arguments
Become familiar with the various detrending methods and some of their arguments

section_blurbs.blurb: Introduction to the notebook's authors and the main focus on filtering and detrending using Pyleoclim.
section_blurbs.heading: Filtering and Detrending with Pyleoclim

section_blurbs.blurb: Outlines the goals, reading time, keywords, and prerequisites for the notebook, emphasizing the use of Pyleoclim for signal processing.
section_blurbs.heading: Preamble

section_blurbs.blurb: Demonstrates detrending methods such as EMD and Savitzky-Golay, showing how to apply them to time series data using Pyleoclim.
section_blurbs.heading: Detrending

section_blurbs.blurb: Covers filtering techniques including Lanczos and Butterworth filters, and illustrates their application to the dataset with visualizations.
section_blurbs.heading: Filtering

inputs: Benthic foraminifera δ18O data from the LR04 benthic stack
outputs: Plots of original and detrended data
